wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Qatar has put a seven-day plan to end the war on the table, and Khamenei, unseen since March, backed Tehran's war conditions; US officials warn Gulf states of strikes after 3 November. Strikes have cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, and an unpublished Pentagon estimate puts the war's cost above $47 billion.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The Iran war reached the tanker lanes: Revolutionary Guards said 3 tankers exploded on Hormuz mines within 24 hours, a day after a Houthi strike claim on a Saudi refinery. The World Bank now expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026, as Vance wrote to Rezaei to restart talks and Trump told Gulf states to 'prepare'.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The rise tracks the war around Iran: the IRGC blockade left Hormuz traffic 11% below normal as of 18 October, and Tehran says three tankers hit mines south of the strait. Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi oil sites, and Ukrainian drones hit oil facilities in St Petersburg.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: Foreign demand for American gas grew: QatarEnergy signed for up to 3 million tonnes a year from Woodside's Louisiana LNG after an Iranian strike on Ras Laffan, and EU gas passed €100 on the Iran war. None of that accounts for the US futures price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The month's wheat news was domestic: Pakistan raised its support price to Rs4,500 a maund, Rs1,000 above last year, after Punjab bought 160,000 tonnes against a 2.5 million target, and its food minister called the price spike manipulated. None of it accounts for the world price, whose latest reading predates those decisions.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Data centres, grid build-out and Chinese stockpiling are competing for the metal, and Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton above London prices. Supply is thinning at the same time: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine, China's smelters are trimming fourth-quarter output, and Rio Tinto's Oyu Tolgoi halted underground operations.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: The Fed held rates, yet markets now fully price a December Fed rate hike, and Warsh's muddled messaging revived doubts about Fed credibility. Higher yields shrink the value of bonds banks already hold: Bank of America's unrealized bond losses rose to $109 billion.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Wall Street's news ran to future supply rather than this window's path: Goldman expects $1.7 trillion of share unlocks in 2027, matched by buybacks, and Walmart and Eli Lilly joined issuers objecting to tokenized shares. The Fed left interest rates unchanged; none of it accounts for the index's moves.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Alphabet's quarterly capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion for AI, turning its free cash flow negative as search missed, and its shares fell about 10% after hours. Anthropic's listing showed $80.7 billion lost on $16.3 billion of revenue. Neither accounts for the slide from the early-October high.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The US reached abroad for relief from surging fuel costs: Trump's deal with Putin sent 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel from Primorsk toward New York, and the US weighed lifting sanctions on Iran's 'shadow fleet'. Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries stopped in mid-October.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: An Iranian strike on Ras Laffan knocked out about 17% of Qatar's LNG capacity, and force majeure on Hormuz cargoes has dragged on, leaving European buyers bidding for scarcer tankers; one Qatari cargo is now crossing the Red Sea toward Poland. The price has since passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The period's news was led by France's school protests turning into a political crisis and by Sudan's deepening fuel shortage. Neither reaches the American stock options this index is built from, and nothing else in the input accounts for the move.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's fortnight was about what imported fuel costs at home. Diesel passed Rs400 a litre, Rs114 of every Rs379.25 litre of petrol is tax, and Energas quit the Port Qasim LNG terminal. Talks between Iran, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan ran alongside. None of it accounts for the rupee's path against the dollar.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news explains the naira's slide. Ebola reached Nigeria, with a confirmed case in Lagos and a patient evacuated to Switzerland. JPMorgan cleared the first step toward a Nigerian bank licence, and Tinubu launched a re-election bid amid economic pain. None of it was reported as moving the exchange rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt moved toward the Houthi war as the pound weakened: parliament, after two postponements, authorised Sisi to defend Saudi Arabia, a step a Houthi figure called a 'declaration of war'. About $18bn of Saudi, Kuwaiti and Qatari deposits make up nearly a third of Egypt's $57bn reserves, and Suez Canal revenue had already fallen to about $4bn.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: News out of Ankara this fortnight was about defence and gas. Turkey submitted the Makkah defence pact to parliament, signed a partnership with Canada and launched its first floating gas platform to double Sakarya field output. None of it accounts for the lira's move against the dollar.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh over these weeks was a draft cyber law, a deadly measles outbreak and Saudi Arabia's execution of two Bangladeshis, and none of it bears on the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah's slide came alongside MSCI's move to remove Indonesia from its global indexes, which forces the funds that track them to sell. Jakarta stocks fell 10% to a six-year low, then 11.6% on a single Friday, the worst day since 1998. Indonesia answered with new measures to improve stock market transparency.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's reporting from Lebanon was about war, not money: Israeli forces bulldozing olive groves around Kfarshouba, and accounts of how years of fighting have deepened Lebanon's cost of living crisis. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan's stories this fortnight were about its reach, not its rate: Bank of China's 2 billion yuan bond in Dubai drew 5 times demand, Hong Kong pitched yuan settlement to Southeast Asia's regional bloc, and three Jiangsu universities moved salaries to the digital yuan. None of it explains the currency's firming.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI was behind the rupee's latest lift: likely central-bank dollar sales on Oct 28 propped up a currency that weakens whenever Brent oil prices rise, since India pays for its crude in dollars.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: Lula's runoff win over the market's pick set off the slide: real futures fell 10% in a Black Monday for Brazil, on worry about the fiscal deficit. Brazilian companies had already fled into dollar stablecoins before the vote, and Flávio Bolsonaro refused to concede a 4.4 million-vote loss, then left for the US.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Mexico's inflation reached 3.62% in early October, above forecasts, but nothing reported over the past weeks explains why the peso weakened against the dollar.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Three strains reached the euro at once: France's borrowing costs hit their highest since 2002 as protests became a political crisis, and European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour. The European Central Bank then held rates with households expecting 3.1% inflation, and Christine Lagarde said she would leave in February.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Doubts about the AI boom sent money into the yen as a safe haven, lifting it to a one-month high of 156.28 per dollar. The same boom pulls the other way, with foreign flows into US equities at a record. At home, the Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate is a 31-year high, and Tokyo is weighing whether wages now drive inflation.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Washington eased pressure on Moscow: Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law, and Witkoff met Putin while Trump pushed Ukraine toward a deal. Ukraine's refinery drone strikes stopped in mid-October, and Russia kept its key rate at 14%, a return that keeps money parked in rubles.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's news this fortnight was fiscal and political rather than monetary: the budget cut the fuel levy until January 2027 over opposition objections, and Merz urged Trump to invite South Africa to the G-20 summit in Miami. None of it accounts for the rand's slide.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The sharpest leg down came with the Binance breach, which Chainalysis confirmed at at least $5.9 billion and blockchain sleuths tie to North Korea's Lazarus Group. About $3 billion was frozen, but 18,270 bitcoin moved into wallets no one can freeze. A day earlier, a dip had already liquidated $356 million in crypto longs.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ethereum fell with the rest of crypto when the Fed held rates with two dissenters seeking a hike and Samsung and Alphabet earnings rattled tech, a drop that liquidated $356 million in crypto longs. Then Binance froze $3 billion in assets after a possible hack that blockchain sleuths tied to North Korea's Lazarus Group.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The slide is the war's oil shock working through interest rates: the World Bank expects global oil supply to fall 5.2% in 2026, energy-led inflation has traders betting on a Fed hike, and the Fed held rates with limited guidance. Gold, which pays no interest, lost 3.6% in one October week, its worst since June.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Late October's AI news was about the bill: Anthropic's listing filing showed it lost $80.7 billion on $16.3 billion of revenue, Alphabet's capex jumped 114% in one quarter and turned its cash flow negative, and Microsoft offered 60,000 buyouts to fund its spending. None of it falls on the mid-month peak.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he signed into law, his envoy Witkoff met Putin, and the Kremlin confirmed talks in Abu Dhabi, where Putin wants a final settlement, not a short truce. Ukraine stopped its refinery drone strikes, and 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel sailed from Primorsk for New York.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say tankers that switched off radar to take an 'unauthorised route' hit mines, seven in one night, as Tehran enforces its own lanes while offering to reopen Hormuz on its conditions. US Central Command says it escorted 1.5 billion barrels; Saudi Arabia will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers hit mines within 24 hours, and Iran threatens Sinokor with legal action from 1 November. An Iranian strike on Ras Laffan and Hormuz force majeure pushed QatarEnergy into buying US gas from Woodside, while Al Gharbia's bypass pipe output fell from 250,000 to 60,000 tonnes.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: This month's Houthi strikes landed on Saudi oil sites, a pipeline and Riyadh airport, and a Qatari gas tanker crossed the Red Sea toward Poland. Egypt, whose Suez Canal revenue fell to about $4bn, had its parliament authorise defending Saudi Arabia; a Houthi figure called that a 'declaration of war'.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: With Hormuz closed, a Qatari gas tanker bound for Poland took the Red Sea route to the canal instead. That route now carries a new risk: Egypt's parliament authorised Sisi to defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, a vote a Houthi figure called a 'declaration of war', on a canal whose revenue had already fallen from $10.2bn in 2023 to about $4bn.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Mines in the Strait of Hormuz set tankers ablaze, Vitol put the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel, and Saudi Arabia agreed to store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027. None of it accounts for the day-to-day vessel count through Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Taipei counted 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, spread in an arc from southern Japan past Taiwan to the Philippines. It was a standing presence across the first island chain, not a one-off drill. That count came after the latest reading, and nothing reported in the fortnight before it explains the fall in transits.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The fortnight's news carried the UN's call to arms over an 'off the charts' El Niño, the pattern behind the drought now killing children in Sudan, but nothing about the canal's water or its transits that accounts for the traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Naval drones have carried the war to merchant shipping off EU coasts. Two ships were hit near Romania, the Khoryv sank off Constanța with one sailor killed, and the Contship Jet went down off Bulgaria after 3 drone hits. Romania blames Russia. None of it has yet thinned the flow through the strait.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The news from either shore of the strait over the fortnight was floods in eastern Spain, the Toledo rail collision and border checks at Ceuta, and none of it touched the shipping that passes between them.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: France spent the fortnight on riots, curfews in Paris and a deal for 200,000 more tonnes of Gulf diesel, and none of it reached the ships moving through the strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Ankara submitted the Makkah defence pact that would bind Turkey to defend Riyadh, Istanbul hosted Iran mediators, and Türkiye warned a fresh assault on Iran risks wider regional war. None of it is about the exchange, and none of it accounts for the slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's news over the slide was a 2027 budget that kept fiscal consolidation going, a ban on civil servants using Waze, a row over Deepavali, and a Tanaka plant to recover gold from chip scrap. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: MSCI moved to cut Indonesia's status and remove it from its global indexes after months of warnings. Jakarta stocks fell 10% to a six-year low, then 11.6% on a Friday, the worst day since 1998. Indonesia answered with new measures to improve stock market transparency.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: AI doubts hit the tech stocks that weigh heavily in the index. The same worries sent investors into the yen as a safe haven, which shrinks what Japan's exporters earn abroad. The Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate, a 31-year high, adds to the yen's pull as Tokyo weighs wage-driven inflation.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Hong Kong's market news was about the listing business itself. The regulator froze HK$4.38 billion over suspected faked public-offering demand, humanoid robot maker Noetix reportedly filed to list, and GOGOX sold its mainland business for 1 yuan. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: China's blue-chip index fell for a record 11 weeks straight as the AI and tech rally repriced: Contemporary Amperex dropped 15% despite a 21.2 billion yuan quarterly profit, and robot shares found no bids at half their valuation. Neither a GDP beat nor the central bank's offer to lend to funds, not just banks, turned it.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The slide ran through two Seoul listings: Elice closed 30% below its offer price amid AI data-centre doubts, and SK hynix shelved a Solidigm listing worth up to $15 billion. The recovery came with growth of 1% last quarter, 3x the forecast, on AI chips, until Samsung's earnings set off a selloff on Thursday.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The fortnight's largest Mumbai event was Jio Platforms' listing: India's largest initial public offering filled in 100 minutes and debuted 21.4% up, leaving Ambani owning the country's top two firms. The central bank also sold dollars to lift the rupee to 95.02. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Indonesia cut its gas exports to Singapore, citing domestic energy needs, in a city where gas generates up to 95% of electricity, and Singapore's top envoy flew to Jakarta after the cuts. At the same time, doubts over AI spread through Asian markets, lifting the yen as a safe haven and knocking 3% off Japan's Nikkei as tech stocks tumbled.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: TSMC, a third of the index, posted record profit for the sixth straight quarter, and its stock fell anyway. The latest session came as Taiwan tracked 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, spread in an arc from southern Japan past Taiwan to the Philippines. Nothing in the input ties either event to the index's path.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to beat Flávio Bolsonaro, the market's pick, and Brazil's Black Monday followed: real futures fell 10% and stocks slumped with the currency. Prices had already risen 4.62% in a year, breaching the inflation ceiling, and companies had moved into dollar stablecoins before the vote.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The one piece of domestic economic news in the window was inflation, which hit 3.62% in early October, above forecasts. Nothing in the input explains the climb from September, or links that reading to share prices.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina's news this fortnight was about investment and the courts: First Quantum sought tax breaks for its $5.25 billion Taca Taca copper mine, a $300 million steelworks in San Nicolás de los Arroyos tested the same incentives, and a court dropped the $LIBRA probe into Milei. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada's biggest stories of the fortnight were political. Albertans voted 76% to stay in Canada, Trump cut 50% tariffs on Canadian crates, boxes and seaweed, and gasoline pushed inflation to 3.1%. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Record foreign flows into US equities rode the AI boom while its cost came due: Alphabet's capex jumped 114% in a quarter and its free cash flow turned negative, and Meta raised $95bn of equity for AI data centres. Intel lost 23% after hours despite beating revenue guidance, and the Fed held rates with markets fully pricing a December hike.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Britain's Budget lifted the tax burden to a record 38.6% of income and scrapped the £108 gas standing charge, while HSBC's quarterly profit jumped 32% and Barclays paired 5,000 job cuts with a £500 million shareholder payout. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: Germany's Ifo expectations index rose for a sixth month, to 91.6 from 90.4, even as loan obstacles reached 7% of euro zone firms. Volkswagen planned zero raises for 660,000 workers until 2030, and the European Central Bank, expected to hold at 2.5%, learned Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's school protests grew into a political crisis, with 410,000 marching on one Saturday and Macron rejecting his interior minister's resignation after riots. Long-term French yields rose from 4% in August to above 5%, and the ECB, squeezed by EU gas above €100 with the Iran war, is heading for a December hike rather than relief.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index leans on ASML, and from Eindhoven its customers are already asking for lithography tools to be delivered in 2029 and 2030, because demand for advanced packaging of AI chips has outrun the machines that make them.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The past fortnight in Spain brought a high-speed collision near Toledo, floods that cut off the east, 25,000 marchers in Madrid demanding pensions that keep pace with inflation, and Milei rallying the far right against Sanchez. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's one market story was a banking one: the ECB cleared Intesa Sanpaolo to bid €32 billion for Monte dei Paschi. It came after the October slide had already turned, and nothing else in the news from Italy, from the air traffic failure to the cost-of-living protests in Milan, accounts for the price.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The fortnight's Swiss market news was the first spot bitcoin ETF on SIX, granted an exemption to hold its coins apart from its manager. Nigeria also evacuated an Ebola patient to Switzerland. Neither reaches the drugmakers and food giant that carry the index, and nothing in the input accounts for its rise.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Israel's news in late October centred on its election, which left neither bloc with 61 seats without Arab parties. It followed Netanyahu's doctrine making preemptive war official policy, and a report that the army chief warned Washington off striking Iran. None of it accounts for the index's path.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The peak came after Trump said the US may strike Iran as soon as Sunday while the Pentagon readied plans, and as prosecutors revived a closed 2016 leak case to charge Comey a third time. Two days later a Trump aide, Simon Levy, confirmed US political asylum for Flávio Bolsonaro after Lula beat him.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed held on Wednesday despite intensifying inflation, after Warsh used a Bangkok appearance to call AI a shock to the economy while withholding guidance. TD Securities had expected 3 dissents; markets now fully price a December hike, and rising yields have lifted Bank of America's unrealized bond losses to $109 billion.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank held this week caught between two shocks pulling opposite ways: bond-market turmoil in France, and EU gas passing €100 as the Iran war lifted energy costs. Households now expect 3.1% inflation, markets are betting on a December hike, and Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027, nine months early.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Its latest leg down ran alongside gold's: gold eased on a firmer dollar ahead of the Fed decision, slipped again when the Fed held rates with limited guidance, and fell once more as higher oil and US inflation data bolstered bets on a hike. A metal that pays no interest loses appeal when rates look set to rise.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged despite the inflation. Days later, higher oil and fresh US inflation data had markets betting on a Fed hike instead, which pulled gold down. Neither report says what pushed prices up in the first place.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Tehran is enforcing its own lanes through the strait by mine: the Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers that took an unauthorised route hit mines within 24 hours, days after they said 2 supertankers carrying 4.5 million barrels had too. Gulf exporters are routing around it: Al Gharbia says every country in the region is considering a pipeline, and Qatar now buys US gas.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: This fortnight's Houthi strikes landed on Saudi soil: Shaybah, a pipeline, a refinery, Dammam's airport. China and Djibouti backed free navigation in the Red Sea, and Egypt voted to defend Saudi Arabia, staking Suez Canal revenue already down from $10.2bn in 2023 to about $4bn. None of it accounts for the rise in transits.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Egypt's parliament authorised Sisi to defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, which puts the canal's own traffic on the line: ships reach it through Bab el-Mandeb, and canal revenue had already fallen from $10.2bn in 2023 to about $4bn. Nothing reported in the window explains the September trough.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: This month's shipping news was elsewhere: Iran threatening transits through Hormuz, concern over the Red Sea, and NATO sending planes and drones to the Black Sea after attacks on shipping. The UN warned of an 'off the charts' El Niño, but nothing reported water restrictions at this canal.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The news of the past fortnight was about the far end of the route Gulf tankers take to Malacca. Iran has been enforcing its own lanes in Hormuz with mines, and Saudi Arabia has arranged to store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027. None of it falls in the weeks this count swung, and none of it explains the swing.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: Taiwan's own map showed 53 Chinese ships, 34 of them warships, spread in an arc from southern Japan past Taiwan to the Philippines. That count came days after the latest reading here, and nothing reported in the window accounts for the swing in commercial traffic.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The shipping news of the fortnight came from the far end of the Gulf route: the Revolutionary Guards say 3 tankers hit mines near Hormuz, and Saudi Arabia is moving crude into storage in Singapore. Torrential rain also battered eastern Spain. Nothing in it ties these events to fewer ships passing Gibraltar.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi missiles killed at least 18 recruits at a Shabwa camp, then drones and missiles reached Saudi Arabia: Shaybah, Dammam airport, a Saudi pipeline. The UK sent Typhoons, the US pulled families from Riyadh, Egypt's parliament voted to defend Saudi Arabia, and Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Washington pushed Kyiv toward a deal: Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he signed into law, Witkoff met Putin, and the Kremlin confirmed talks in Abu Dhabi. Under US pressure, Ukraine stopped its refinery drone strikes in mid-October, and Starlink throttling cut its drones' links.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple Intelligence reached China in beta, running on Alibaba's Qwen models, and the iPhone Duo was backordered until 2027 as pre-order sales soared, though Apple's foldable phone drew complaints about a crease. Then came the M6 MacBook Pro: a touchscreen with OLED, up to 24 hours of battery, from $1,999.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results showed a revenue miss, which it put down to weak search, and capital spending up 114% to $51.4 billion in a single quarter, mostly on AI. That spending turned free cash flow negative. The search advertising that pays for the build-out fell short of expectations while the bill for it more than doubled.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's own news in the fortnight was hardware: AI devices that listen to conversations, then new Alexa devices including a 16-Inch Echo smart display and an Alexa photo frame. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: TSMC reported a record profit for the sixth straight quarter, and the shares fell on the news rather than rising. Nothing in the input explains why a record result met selling.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, cutting payroll to pay for data centres. It also dropped the Nscale site at Loughton because grid power there may wait a decade. Neither story explains the price.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX's revenue doubled last quarter, but it spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure and has borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly in callable debt. In Ukraine, officials say Starlink cuts out at 130 km/h, and the Pentagon inspector general declined a nine-senator probe into those limits.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta lost a New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica that cost it $25 billion, and AI spending left the quarter's free cash flow negative $2.12 billion. It then created nonvoting shares and moved to sell $95bn of stock, its largest ever, to fund AI data centres; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eye up to $5 billion of it.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Yemen's Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, Iran's state agency Mehr reported, and four days later a Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field sent Brent crude to $110.63. Saudi Arabia cancelled its 2026 'Davos in the Desert' amid the attacks, and will store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Two bets on Tesla's future outweighed its present. It debuted the 2026 Roadster, a sports car priced from $200,000, and it was reported to be exploring a merger with SpaceX that would hold 30,000 BTC. Its third-quarter results did not undo either: net profit fell 43% to $787 million.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung's earnings rattled tech stocks on Thursday, and the selloff on the Kospi ended a week in which its memory-chip business had lifted the shares about 8%. The same day it was reported to be pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong, months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market to Chinese brands.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan struck at Taoyuan as a dispute over bonuses escalated. Nothing reported about the walkout, or anything else about the company's own business, accounts for the share price.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: The fortnight's news about Lilly's own business was Belgium refusing to cover Mounjaro, and the company joining Walmart and 36 others in opting out of OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares. Neither accounts for the rise.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: The CBN granted JPMorgan approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, the first licensing step for a firm present in Lagos since 1961, and the bank said lenders are done financing AI on faith. Neither touches the earnings behind the share, and nothing else here accounts for its price.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK hynix shelved a listing of Solidigm, its NAND storage arm, worth up to $15 billion, while its own record US listing traded underwater. The pulled offering came as the company leaned harder on AI storage, and ahead of its earnings it led a rise in chip stocks.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: Walmart joined Eli Lilly and 36 other issuers in objecting to OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares. The dispute is over who controls shareholder records and price discovery, and nothing in it accounts for the share's rise.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Lithography tools have sold out: customers are now asking ASML for machines to be delivered in 2029 and 2030. Its order book is spoken for years ahead, as demand from advanced packaging for AI chips outruns what it can build.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The one Solana story of the fortnight was about its security, not its price: 809 submissions, many of them AI-generated spam, swamped its $1 million bug contest, and filing a report now costs 1 SOL. Nothing in it accounts for the token's slide.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: Ripple won final approval for its own U.S. national trust bank, and Franklin Templeton added $150 million of money-market shares to the XRP Ledger, yet neither lifted the token. It fell with the market as altcoins slid, bitcoin dipped below $80,000 and liquidated $356 million in longs, and a Binance hack sent prices lower again.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: The only reports on the token in the window were two single-day jumps, of 11% and then 8%, each a line in a Bitcoin market wrap: one alongside AI earnings reviving tech, the other ahead of a Fed decision. Neither gave a cause specific to Zcash, and nothing in the input explains the slide from its late-September high.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: Nothing in the fortnight explains a change in the rate. Bank of England policymaker Greene said inflation risks are bigger than thought, and gas drove £161 of a £180 rise in UK electricity bills, the kind of energy shock that has prompted the question of why a central bank might hike rather than cut.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The rate is at a 31-year high, and the case for going further built through October: Ueda said the Bank of Japan could not tolerate underlying inflation running further over 2%, the IMF said the BOJ would have to tighten faster if inflation beat its forecast, and the finance minister said Japan was shifting to a wage-driven inflation phase.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China has been acting through levers other than this rate. It plans a bond-market liquidity backstop that lends to funds, not just banks, and is piloting onshore yuan trade for foreign banks. It also bought 23 tonnes of gold in September.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's Board of Directors held the key rate at its October meeting and named high inflation expectations as its point of concern. The regulator credited rising export revenues with backing the ruble, which slowed after the decision. Through the month it kept buying yuan, roughly $150 mln with each settlement.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Bangkok hosted the IMF and World Bank meetings, where Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and the European Central Bank headed for a December hike, but none of it concerned Thai companies. Inflation and an energy crisis were squeezing Southeast Asian households, though nothing in the reporting ties either to the index.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The Houthi campaign reached Saudi oil itself: a drone strike on Shaybah, missiles over Yanbu and a claimed hit on the pipeline, after the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell. Riyadh postponed its investor summit to 2027. The selling eased once Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: News from the Emirates ran on the Hormuz war. Non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter, and the Al Gharbia pipeline built to bypass the strait fell from 250,000 to 60,000 tonnes. Neither ties the late-October trough to a single event on the Dubai market.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Inflation reached 7.2% in September against a 2-4% target, and the central bank answered with a half-point rate hike, raising what Philippine firms and households pay to borrow. Oil above $110 after a Houthi drone strike near the Saudi Shaybah field fed the same squeeze through the import bill and a weak peso.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta lost the New Mexico case over Cambridge Analytica, a $25 billion penalty, and its quarter showed AI spending pushing free cash flow to negative $2.12 billion. It then created nonvoting shares Wall Street called an overhang and planned a $95 billion stock sale to fund AI data centres.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year, the money going into AI data centres. Earlier it walked away from Nscale's planned AI site at Loughton, where grid power may not arrive until the 2030s.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The fortnight's news about Tencent was product news: 2,000 free search calls a month for developers building AI agents, the WorkBuddy agent added to WeCom, Lvpaopao's short dramas at 143 million monthly users, and a preview of Hunyuan Hy4. None of it explains the share price.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon pledged €16 billion in Germany, split between data centers and its Prime business, which added to its cloud capacity in Europe's largest economy. Days earlier it launched AI devices built to hear and keep track of conversations, pushing Alexa further into the home.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: SpaceX spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure last quarter and has borrowed $40 billion for GPUs, mostly callable debt, as Musk warned of a neocloud shakeout. In Ukraine, drones lost Starshield links above 160 km/h for 10 days, and the Pentagon inspector general declined a nine-senator Starlink probe.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia, with AMD and Broadcom, eyed up to $5 billion of Meta's $95bn share sale, money Meta is raising to build AI data centres. iFlytek said it trained Spark X2.6 without Nvidia, and Google's rival chip lifted its cloud sales. None of it accounts for the slide in the share.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The fighting ran the other way: Houthi missiles targeted Saudi oil routes at Yanbu and the East-West pipeline, threatened Riyadh's airport, killed 18 recruits at a Shabwa camp and struck at Aden. Egypt voted to defend Saudi Arabia and the UK expanded its support, but nothing reported a ground push on Sanaa.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: The Houthis escalated instead of standing down. They hit Aden and Saudi sites, fired 10 ballistic missiles at a Saudi pipeline, declared Riyadh's airport a military target and claimed a refinery strike. Egypt's parliament voted to defend Saudi Arabia. The one diplomatic meeting ran through Tehran, where Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthis have been firing on Saudi Arabia's oil sites, claiming hits on a pipeline and a refinery, the latter lifting Brent to $115.36, and say Saudi strikes killed 16 people in Aden. Riyadh has gathered allies: Pakistan ratified the Makkah defence pact, Egypt's parliament voted to defend it, and its defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: Through October Washington pushed for a Ukraine deal. Witkoff headed to Russia, Trump urged Kyiv to settle, and Ukraine stopped its refinery drone strikes under US pressure, while Lavrov said the war would continue and likely escalate. None of it involved Xi, and nothing in the reporting points to the three leaders meeting.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 2. Its price is what traders will stake on a deal that would reopen the Gulf's main oil export route.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Washington warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November, and an Iranian official called Qatar's seven-day plan 'unacceptable' while Araghchi said Tehran stayed 'in contact' with mediators. The Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines on an 'unauthorised route', Tehran enforcing its own lanes rather than negotiating them.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the war pausing this year.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-decem.recent: Bets firmed as Trump put new Russia sanctions on hold, sent Witkoff to Putin and pressed Kyiv to cut a deal, and the Kremlin confirmed talks in Abu Dhabi. But Putin said he wanted a final settlement, not a "short" truce, and Lavrov then said the war would continue and likely escalate.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results came out after the chart's last close. Capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion for AI capacity, which turned free cash flow negative even as Google Cloud revenue doubled. Search revenue missed, and the shares fell about 10% after hours.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: Bets fell as the war widened. The Houthis said Saudi strikes killed 16 people, then claimed a strike on a Saudi pipeline as air defences intercepted 10 ballistic missiles, and declared Riyadh's airport a military target. Prices picked up after Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran.

wiki-france.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on France each day. Its peaks mark the days events in the country reached people well beyond its borders.
wiki-france.recent: France's school protests turned into a political crisis: police arrested nearly 2,400 people in one night, partial curfews began at 11pm, and Macron rejected his interior minister's resignation. France's 10-year bond yield reached 4.96%, its highest since 2002, and a gunman in Trappes killed 1 in a suspected Islamophobic shooting.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Bets on a handover firmed as channels reopened: Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Rezaei, Qatar tabled a seven-day plan to end the war, and Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president. Against that, Khamenei backed Tehran's war conditions and Washington warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November.

stocks:300750.SZ.standing: Contemporary Amperex Technology, the Ningde company listed in Shenzhen and the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries. Carmakers from Tesla to BYD's rivals buy its cells, so its share tracks the EV and grid-storage build-out.
stocks:300750.SZ.recent: Contemporary Amperex reported a quarterly profit of 21.2 billion yuan, and its shares still fell 15%. The drop came as China's tech stocks were repriced, with investors weighing earnings against valuations, so a strong quarter did not protect the stock.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats control the US Senate after the 2026 midterm elections. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet officers, so whoever holds it decides who a president can appoint.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The fortnight brought charges against former FBI officials over their 2023 testimony, landing 11 days before the midterms, and a CFTC suit against Utah to protect Kalshi and other prediction markets from a gambling ban. Neither accounts for what traders now pay on control of the Senate.

poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Banco de México cuts its overnight rate by a quarter point after November. That rate sets borrowing costs across Mexico and the yield gap that draws foreign money into the peso.
poly-bank-of-mexico-decreases-interest-r.recent: No story in the fortnight came from Banxico itself. The news was Washington's: the Fed under Warsh held rates and markets moved to price a December Fed hike, which narrows the room for a Banxico cut, but none of it accounts for this contract's swings.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.
poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.recent: Venezuelans marched in Caracas on Thursday demanding that a presidential election date be set, which is the outcome this contract pays on. Nothing in the reporting shows any date being named, and none of it explains why traders cut what they will pay.

poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between the United States and Iran survives until the US midterm elections. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, threats and mediation.
poly-us-iran-ceasefire-continues-through.recent: Saudi Arabia's defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, and Khamenei, unseen since March, backed Tehran's peace conditions. Then Vance wrote to Iran's security chief Rezaei, Qatar tabled a seven-day plan, and US officials warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November, the midterm date this contract runs to.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: South Korea's second-largest chipmaker and one of the world's two biggest makers of memory chips. It leads in high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM beside AI accelerators, so its shares trade on AI data-centre spending.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: SK hynix shelved a listing of Solidigm, its NAND storage arm, that would have raised up to $15 billion, while its own record US listing was trading underwater. Most of the slide came before that decision, and nothing in the input about the company's own business accounts for it.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Texas's US Senate race in November 2026. Texas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1988, so the price shows how far traders bet against that record.

poly-cuban-regime-falls-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Cuba's communist government loses power before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set against a one-party state that has outlasted decades of US sanctions.

wiki-flavio-bolsonaro.standing: The daily readership of the Wikipedia article on Flávio Bolsonaro, the Rio de Janeiro senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who carries his father's movement on Brazil's right.
wiki-flavio-bolsonaro.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to win the runoff by 4.4 million votes, after polls had put Bolsonaro narrowly ahead. Bolsonaro then left Brazil through no regular border post, and Trump aide Simon Levy confirmed political asylum for him in the US, a flight Lula called shameful.

stocks:JPM.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, spanning Chase's consumer branches, corporate lending and one of Wall Street's biggest investment banks. Its results are read as a check on American borrowers.
stocks:JPM.recent: The one development in the bank's own business was the CBN granting it approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, where it has operated from Lagos since 1961. That is the first licensing step for a small new market, and nothing in it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Tinubu opened his re-election campaign in Kaduna with petrol at about 1,400 naira a litre in September, the economic pain any challenger runs against, and Microsoft pledged to load Nigeria's candidate list into its AI systems. Both stories came after the days the price moved, and neither accounts for it.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that settles at 100 if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race. Ohio has leaned Republican in recent statewide contests, so the seat bears on which party controls the Senate.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the 2026 midterm elections. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and House control decides whether a president's agenda can pass.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: In the run-up to the midterms, charges were filed in Washington against former FBI officials over their 2023 testimony, landing 11 days before the vote. Nothing else in the fortnight's news bore on the House race, and none of it moved what traders will pay on a Democratic majority.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.
